series.label: Least-cost healthy diet per person per day, PPP
series.unit: current PPP international dollars per representative person per day
series.price_basis: source year-specific private-consumption PPP; 2021 ICP benchmark food prices updated using national food CPI
series.interpretation: Published FAO/World Bank estimate of the least expensive locally available foods meeting the healthy-diet basket at 2,330 kcal/day. It is a modeled benchmark, not actual household food expenditure or a universal individual dietary prescription.
series.adjustment: Published source value; no local conversion, interpolation or inflation adjustment
series.estimate_note: Published compiled or modeled estimate; blank source status does not certify direct measurement.
series.definition:
The cost of a healthy diet indicator is the cost of purchasing the least expensive locally available foods to meet requirements for energy and food-based dietary guidelines (FBDG) for a representative person within energy balance at 2330 kcal/day. The cost of a healthy diet is converted to international dollars using purchasing power parity (PPP). Data are available for the period from 2017 and 2025. 

For Bahamas, Guyana, Haiti, Iran, Myanmar, and Sint Maarten (Dutch Part), retail food prices were not available from the ICP 2021. As a result, the CoHD for these countries is calculated using data from the ICP 2017.

For Bahamas, Guyana, Haiti, Iran, Myanmar, and Sint Maarten (Dutch Part), retail food prices were not available from the ICP 2021. As a result, the CoHD for these countries is calculated using data from the ICP 2017.

Adapted from Herforth, A., Venkat, A., Bai, Y., Costlow, L., Holleman, C. & Masters, W.A. 2022. Methods and options to monitor the cost and affordability of a healthy diet globally. series.label: Population unable to afford a healthy diet, published estimate
series.price_basis: source modeled affordability using food costs, income distributions and basic non-food allowances
series.interpretation: Published modeled prevalence, accounting for an allowance for basic non-food needs. Zero may mean a positive estimate rounded down at source precision. This is not a locally calculated residual household budget.
series.adjustment: Published source value; no local conversion, interpolation or inflation adjustment
series.estimate_note: Published compiled or modeled estimate; blank source status does not certify direct measurement. Native API long-definition text mentions an energy-sufficient diet under the healthy-diet indicator title; the source programme methods distinguish diet standards. This wording discrepancy is preserved and documented. Publisher metadata has a wording inconsistency: the indicator title identifies healthy-diet unaffordability, while its retained long definition refers to energy-sufficient food. Consult the original metadata and source guide before interpreting the threshold.
series.definition: The indicator estimates the percentage of individuals in a population whose disposable income, net of the amount needed to acquire basic non-food goods and services, is lower than the average cost of the least-expensive energy sufficient diet in a country. The expenditures for basic non-food needs are calculated as average non-food expenditure shares of low-income consumers multipled by internaitonal poverty lines set by the World Bank. The non-food expenditure share is 37% and 44% in low-income and lower-middle-income countries for the second quintile of consumers, and 54% in upper-middle-and-high-income countries for the first quintile of consumers, according to household surveys compiled by the World Bank. The international poverty lines are $3/day for low-income countries, $4.2/day for lower-middle-income countries, $8.3/day for upper-middle-income countries, and $29.43/day for high-income countries, in 2021PPP$. Countries' income classifications follow the calendar year of 2024 standard (fiscal year of 2026 of the World Bank). Income data are provided by the World Bank’s Poverty and Inequality Platform. A value of zero indicates a null or a small number rounded down at the current precision level. Data available from 2017 to 2025.

sources.title: OECD annual household consumption by purpose · COICOP 2018
OECD annual household consumption by purpose · COICOP 1999

limitations: These global context measures are not components of a matched income-minus-essentials residual. Denominators, sources and price bases remain separate.
Current international-dollar healthcare and diet costs are not constant-2021 welfare values. No local PPP or inflation conversion is applied.
Out-of-pocket health share means share of total current health expenditure, not share of household income.
Healthy-diet costs are least-cost modeled benchmarks for a representative 2,330 kcal/day person, not actual food expenditure or a universal individual nutrition prescription.
Food source FPN 5.0 (July 2026) uses updated income/poverty conventions; the archived July 2025 method brief describes price updating but is not the authority for the 2026 poverty thresholds.
National averages do not describe each household. Missing source cells remain missing; no local interpolation, nearest-year substitution, or zero replacement is used.
OECD domestic category shares are ratios of category expenditure to total domestic household consumption, not shares of resident income. They do not supply an income remainder.
COICOP 2018 and COICOP 1999 share series remain separate. Current national-currency amounts cancel within the same country/year ratio; currencies are never treated as equal amounts.
Healthcare-purpose consumption follows national-account financing conventions. It is distinct from out-of-pocket healthcare and should not be presented as a household cash bill.

For original World Bank/FAO records, source_record_ref resolves relative to global_context/ in the source ZIP. Added OECD references resolve relative to the ZIP root; source_record_base records this explicitly.
